rv.q: Under the direction of Jonathan James, the company offers a very good production of a play whose flaws result in an unsatisfying narrative.
These factors made it harder to connect with the characters and diminished the impact of the final scenes, which are meant to be emotionally charged.
The same could be said of this production: it’s an interesting mess—but a mess nonetheless.
This is Shanley’s hymn, perhaps to himself, which gives a brilliant perspective on growing up body and soul in the combustible and impossible years of adolescence.

cn.t: Shanley's autobiographical coming-of-age drama earns mixed notices: critics praise its rich textures and strong production, but find the narrative ultimately unsatisfying. A slow-burn with potential that doesn't fully deliver.
